claims.claim: Arrived Queenstown (about ten o'clock this morning)
claims.citation: New York Herald, 23 May 1866, p. 11, col. 4
claims.verbatim:
Steamship City of Washington—Queenstown, May 7—
The missing steamer City of Washington, of the Inman line,
was towed into this port about ten o'clock this morning by
the City of Cork, another steamer owned by the same com-
pany.

May 7, at 9 a. m., the steamship City of Washington, arrived at
Queenstown with loss of rudder, and in tow of steamship City of
Cork, having been towed 1,002[?] miles.

THE STEAMER CITY OF WASHINGTON HEARD
FROM.—A telegraphic despatch received here
this morning conveys the gratifying intelli-
gence that foreign advices to the 29th ult. (two
days later than published this morniug) have
been received at New York, announcing the
arrival out of the steamer Propontis with the
passengers of the City of Washington, having
overtaken the latter steamer disabled and
under sail.
